claim: Actinonin is an anti-bacterial and anti-parasitic antibiotic derived from streptomycete bacteria.
source: Actinonin is an anti-bacterial and anti-parasitic antibiotic derived from streptomycete bacteria (Gordon et al., 1962; Wiesner et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gordon et al., 1962 and Wiesner et al., 2001

claim: In bacteria, actinonin targets peptide deformylase (PDF).
source: In bacteria, actinonin targets peptide deformylase (PDF) (Chen et al., 2000)
evidence: Supported by citation to Chen et al., 2000

claim: Actinonin causes defects in malaria parasite apicoplast development.
source: Actinonin causes defects in malaria parasite apicoplast development (Goodman and McFadden, 2014)
evidence: Supported by citation to Goodman and McFadden, 2014

claim: Actinonin inhibits recombinantly expressed Plasmodium falciparum PDF (PfPDF – PF3D7_0907900) in vitro at concentrations consistent with its anti-parasitic activity.
source: inhibits recombinantly expressed Plasmodium falciparum PDF (PfPDF – PF3D7_0907900) in vitro (Bracchi-Ricard et al., 2001) at concentrations consistent with its anti-parasitic activity
evidence: Supported by citation to Bracchi-Ricard et al., 2001

claim: The characteristics of actinonin—particularly the rapid mode of action and the unusual kinetics of apicoplast genome loss—are at odds with how all other drugs targeting apicoplast translation impact the parasite.
source: However, the characteristics of actinonin —particularly the rapid mode of action and the unusual kinetics of apicoplast genome loss —are at odds with how all other drugs targeting apicoplast translation impact the parasite (Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017; Uddin et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017 and Uddin et al., 2018

claim: Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017 identified a point mutation in the putative metalloprotease TgftsH1 that confers a 3.5-fold resistance to actinonin in Toxoplasma gondii.
source: In a search for the target of actinonin, Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017 used the related apicomplexan Toxoplasma gondii and identified a point mutation in the putative metalloprotease TgftsH1 that confers a 3.5-fold resistance to actinonin.
evidence: Supported by citation to Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017

claim: Actinonin inhibits recombinantly expressed human malaria parasite FtsH1 (PfFtsH1) in vitro at levels comparable to its antimalarial activity.
source: They also showed that actinonin inhibits recombinantly expressed human malaria parasite FtsH1 (PfFtsH1) in vitro at levels comparable to its antimalarial activity (Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017

claim: Parasites with reduced PfFtsH1 expression were more sensitive to actinonin.
source: Moreover, parasites with reduced PfFtsH1 expression were more sensitive to actinonin, all of which prompted the interim conclusion that PfFtsH1, rather than PfPDF, might be the target of actinonin and that PfFtsH1 is a potential new antimalarial target (Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017

claim: Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017 were not able to generate actinonin resistant P. falciparum parasites despite repeated attempts.
source: Despite repeated attempts, Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017 were not able to generate actinonin resistant P. falciparum parasites.
evidence: Supported by citation to Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017

claim: The residue mutated from asparagine to serine (N805S) in TgFtsH1 that confers actinonin resistance is already a serine in PfFtsH1.
source: Interestingly, the residue mutated from asparagine to serine (N805S) in TgFtsH1 identified as conferring actinonin resistance by Amberg-Johnson et al. (Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017) is already a serine in PfFtsH1 (Table 1)
evidence: Supported by citation to Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017 and data shown in Table 1

claim: PfFtsH1 is localized in the mitochondrion.
source: Compounding this uncertainty is a report that PfFtsH1 is localized in the mitochondrion (Tanveer et al., 2013)
evidence: Supported by citation to Tanveer et al., 2013

claim: Phenotypic evidence from PfFtsH1 knockdowns and changes in post-translational processing of PfFtsH1 in the absence of a functioning apicoplast strongly suggest a relationship between PfFtsH1 and the apicoplast.
source: However, phenotypic evidence from PfFtsH1 knockdowns and changes in post-translational processing of PfFtsH1 in the absence of a functioning apicoplast (Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017) strongly suggest a relationship between PfFtsH1 and the apicoplast.
evidence: Supported by citation to Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017

claim: There is a close physical and functional association between the mitochondria and apicoplast in malaria parasites.
source: These contradictory findings may result from the of differential targeting of the various processed forms of PfFtsH1 (Tanveer et al., 2013) or stem from the close physical and functional association between the mitochondria and apicoplast in malaria parasites (van Dooren et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to van Dooren et al., 2005

claim: P. falciparum strain D10 parasites were selected for actinonin resistance using stepwise increases in actinonin concentration starting with 10 million parasites treated with 2 µM of actinonin.
source: P. falciparum strain D10 parasites were selected for resistance using stepwise increases in actinonin concentration. Ten million parasites were treated with 2 µM of actinonin
evidence: Describes the experimental methodology used in this study

claim: Treatment with 2 µM actinonin resulted in no parasites being detectable in the culture by microscopy.
source: Ten million parasites were treated with 2 µM of actinonin, which resulted in no parasites being detectable in the culture by microscopy.
evidence: Reports experimental observation from this study

claim: Parasites were cultured with stepwise increases in actinonin concentration until they grew vigorously in media containing 20 µM actinonin.
source: Drug concentration was then increased two-fold and the process repeated until parasites were growing vigorously in media containing 20 µM actinonin.
evidence: Describes experimental results from this study

claim: Several clones generated from the actinonin resistant parasite line showed IC50 values 18 to 35-fold higher than the parental line.
source: Several clones were generated from our actinonin resistant parasite line, and each showed consistent actinonin resistance, with IC50 values 18 to 35-fold higher than the parental line (Table 1, Supplementary file 1a).
evidence: Reports experimental data from this study shown in Table 1 and Supplementary file 1a

claim: The clone with the highest level of resistance showed an IC50 of 73.3 µM actinonin.
source: The clone with the highest level of resistance showed an IC50 of 73.3 µM actinonin (Table 1, Figure 1B,C).
evidence: Reports experimental data from this study shown in Table 1 and Figure 1B,C

claim: Four actinonin resistant clones retained wild type sequences of Pf pdf, Pf formyl-methionyl transferase (Pffmt - PF3D7_1313200), and Pf methionyl amino peptidase (Pfmap - PF3D7_0804400).
source: We genotyped four actinonin resistant clones and all retained wild type sequences of Pf pdf, Pf formyl-methionyl transferase (Pffmt - PF3D7_1313200), and Pf methionyl amino peptidase (Pfmap - PF3D7_0804400)
evidence: Reports experimental genotyping results from this study

claim: All four actinonin resistant clones retained wild type sequence for PfRING (PF3D7_1405700).
source: Similarly, all four actinonin resistant clones retained wild type sequence for PfRING (PF3D7_1405700), another actinonin target candidate (Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017).
evidence: Reports experimental genotyping results from this study, with citation to Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017 for PfRING being a candidate target

claim: Each of the four actinonin resistant clones harbors a single nucleotide polymorphism in Pfftsh1 that changed amino acid 489 from glycine to cysteine.
source: However, each of the clones harbors a single nucleotide polymorphism in Pfftsh1 that changed amino acid 489 (adjacent TgFtsH1 N805S) from glycine to cysteine (Table 1, Supplementary file 1a)
evidence: Reports experimental genotyping results from this study shown in Table 1 and Supplementary file 1a

claim: The G489C mutation in PfFtsH1 is adjacent to the TgFtsH1 N805S mutation.
source: However, each of the clones harbors a single nucleotide polymorphism in Pfftsh1 that changed amino acid 489 (adjacent TgFtsH1 N805S) from glycine to cysteine (Table 1, Supplementary file 1a)
evidence: Reports the relationship between mutations based on sequence analysis shown in Table 1

claim: The presence of the G489C mutation in all four resistant clones strongly implies that PfFtsH1 is the primary target of actinonin.
source: However, each of the clones harbors a single nucleotide polymorphism in Pfftsh1 that changed amino acid 489 (adjacent TgFtsH1 N805S) from glycine to cysteine (Table 1, Supplementary file 1a), strongly implying that PfFtsH1 is the primary target of actinonin.
evidence: Inference drawn from the experimental data showing consistent mutation in all resistant clones

claim: A parasite clone carrying synonymous 'shield' mutations in the Pfftsh1 coding sequence but retaining glycine 489 (rFtsH1G489G) remained sensitive to actinonin.
source: Accordingly, a parasite clone carrying synonymous 'shield' mutations in the Pfftsh1 coding sequence designed to prevent ongoing Cas9 cleavage but retaining glycine 489 (rFtsH1G489G) remained sensitive to actinonin (Figure 1B,C, Supplementary file 1b)
evidence: Reports experimental results from CRISPR-Cas9 editing shown in Figure 1B,C and Supplementary file 1b

claim: Two independent clones (rFtsH1G489Ca/b) modified to have the G489C mutation showed actinonin resistance levels comparable to the actinonin-selected line (wtACTR).
source: whereas two independent clones (rFtsH1G489Ca/b) modified to have the G489C mutation (in addition to the 'shield' mutations) showed actinonin resistance levels comparable to the actinonin-selected line (wtACTR) (Figure 1B,C, Supplementary file 1b).
evidence: Reports experimental results from CRISPR-Cas9 editing shown in Figure 1B,C and Supplementary file 1b

claim: The G489C mutation in PfFtsH1 confirms that PfFtsH1 is the primary target of actinonin.
source: Robust actinonin resistance in P. falciparum resulting from the G489C mutation confirms that PfFtsH1 is indeed the primary target of actinonin.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing that introducing the G489C mutation confers resistance

claim: The resistance levels in PfFtsH1 G489C parasites are of the same order of magnitude as that seen in lines that lack an apicoplast.
source: That the resistance levels in PfFtsH1 G489C parasites are of the same order of magnitude as that seen in lines that lack an apicoplast (Table 1)
evidence: Comparison of experimental data shown in Table 1

claim: The comparable resistance levels between PfFtsH1 G489C parasites and apicoplast-minus parasites strengthens the conclusion that PfFtsH1 has a role in apicoplast biogenesis.
source: That the resistance levels in PfFtsH1 G489C parasites are of the same order of magnitude as that seen in lines that lack an apicoplast (Table 1), strengthens the conclusion that PfFtsH1 has a role in apicoplast biogenesis, the anomalous localization (Tanveer et al., 2013) notwithstanding.
evidence: Inference drawn from comparison of experimental data, with citation to Tanveer et al., 2013 regarding localization

claim: Greater levels of resistance achievable through prolonged selection suggests that these lines may have acquired other mutations that compensate for reduced PfFtsH1 function and/or alter secondary actinonin targets.
source: The greater levels of resistance achievable through prolonged selection, while modest, suggests that these lines may have acquired other mutations that compensate for reduced PfFtsH1 function and/or alter secondary actinonin targets, such as the other metalloproteases present in the genome (Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017).
evidence: Speculative interpretation of the data regarding additional mutations, with citation to Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017 regarding other metalloproteases

claim: The ability to generate resistance to actinonin in a relatively small starting population of P. falciparum parasites means actinonin is not an 'irresistible' drug.
source: Our ability to generate resistance to actinonin in a relatively small starting population of P. falciparum parasites means actinonin is not an 'irresistible' drug (Cowell and Winzeler, 2018)
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental results, with citation to Cowell and Winzeler, 2018 regarding the concept of 'irresistible' drugs

claim: The ease of generating actinonin resistance tempers enthusiasm for development of PfFtsH1 as an antimalarial target.
source: Our ability to generate resistance to actinonin in a relatively small starting population of P. falciparum parasites means actinonin is not an 'irresistible' drug (Cowell and Winzeler, 2018), which tempers enthusiasm for development of PfFtsH1 as an antimalarial target.
evidence: Inference drawn from the experimental finding that resistance can be readily generated

claim: The selection procedure to generate actinonin resistant parasites required 10 weeks of constant drug selection to recover resistant parasites.
source: This selection procedure required 10 weeks of constant drug selection to recover resistant parasites and 10 months of selection to develop parasites with the highest levels of resistance.
evidence: Reports the timeline of the experimental selection procedure

claim: The selection procedure required 10 months of selection to develop parasites with the highest levels of resistance.
source: This selection procedure required 10 weeks of constant drug selection to recover resistant parasites and 10 months of selection to develop parasites with the highest levels of resistance.
evidence: Reports the timeline of the experimental selection procedure

claim: The parasite strain and selection methodology used in this study differ from previous attempts to generate resistance.
source: Both the parasite strain and selection methodology used differ from previous attempts to generate resistance (Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017), which may explain why we obtained resistance where others did not.
evidence: Comparison with previous work cited from Amberg-Johnson et al., 2017

claim: Actinonin kills malaria parasites (Plasmodium falciparum) by interfering with apicoplast function.
source: The antibiotic actinonin kills malaria parasites (Plasmodium falciparum) by interfering with apicoplast function.
evidence: Statement from the abstract summarizing established knowledge

claim: Early evidence suggested that actinonin inhibited prokaryote-like post-translational modification in the apicoplast, mimicking its activity against bacteria.
source: Early evidence suggested that actinonin inhibited prokaryote-like post-translational modification in the apicoplast; mimicking its activity against bacteria.
evidence: Statement from the abstract summarizing previous understanding

claim: Amberg Johnson et al. (2017) identified the metalloprotease TgFtsH1 as the target of actinonin in Toxoplasma gondii.
source: However, Amberg Johnson et al. (2017) identified the metalloprotease TgFtsH1 as the target of actinonin in the related parasite Toxoplasma gondii
evidence: Supported by citation to Amberg Johnson et al. (2017)

claim: Amberg Johnson et al. (2017) implicated P. falciparum FtsH1 as a likely target of actinonin in malaria parasites.
source: Amberg Johnson et al. (2017) identified the metalloprotease TgFtsH1 as the target of actinonin in the related parasite Toxoplasma gondii and implicated P. falciparum FtsH1 as a likely target in malaria parasites.
evidence: Supported by citation to Amberg Johnson et al. (2017)

claim: Amberg Johnson et al. (2017) were not able to recover actinonin resistant malaria parasites, leaving the specific target of actinonin uncertain.
source: The authors were not, however, able to recover actinonin resistant malaria parasites, leaving the specific target of actinonin uncertain.
evidence: Statement from the abstract referring to previous work

claim: This study generated actinonin resistant P. falciparum by in vitro selection.
source: We generated actinonin resistant P. falciparum by in vitro selection
evidence: Statement from the abstract describing the experimental approach

claim: This study identified a specific sequence change in PfFtsH1 associated with actinonin resistance.
source: We generated actinonin resistant P. falciparum by in vitro selection and identified a specific sequence change in PfFtsH1 associated with resistance.
evidence: Statement from the abstract describing the experimental findings

claim: Introduction of the G489C point mutation using CRISPR-Cas9 allelic replacement was sufficient to confer actinonin resistance in P. falciparum.
source: Introduction of this point mutation using CRISPr-Cas9 allelic replacement was sufficient to confer actinonin resistance in P. falciparum.
evidence: Statement from the abstract describing the experimental validation

claim: The data unequivocally identify PfFtsH1 as the target of actinonin.
source: Our data unequivocally identify PfFtsH1 as the target of actinonin
evidence: Conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study

claim: Actinonin should not be included in the collection of 'irresistible' drugs for combatting malaria.
source: Our data unequivocally identify PfFtsH1 as the target of actinonin and suggests that actinonin should not be included in the highly valuable collection of 'irresistible' drugs for combatting malaria.
evidence: Recommendation based on the finding that resistance can be readily generated

claim: Peptide deformylase (PDF) is an enzyme involved in prokaryotic post-translational modification.
source: In bacteria, actinonin targets peptide deformylase (PDF) (Chen et al., 2000), an enzyme involved in prokaryotic post-translational modification
evidence: Established knowledge about PDF function, with citation to Chen et al., 2000

claim: Peptide deformylase is present in the relict plastid (apicoplast) of apicomplexan parasites.
source: In bacteria, actinonin targets peptide deformylase (PDF) (Chen et al., 2000), an enzyme involved in prokaryotic post-translational modification and also present in the relict plastid (apicoplast) of apicomplexan parasites.
evidence: Established knowledge about the presence of PDF in the apicoplast

claim: The general conclusion was that actinonin targets the apicoplast-localized PfPDF in malaria parasites.
source: all of which led to the general conclusion that actinonin targets the apicoplast-localized PfPDF in malaria parasites.
evidence: Statement summarizing previous scientific consensus
